messages:
Ana: quick thought — after the last postmortem I put together a tiny follow-up checklist + a compact timeline template. want to avoid the usual 'actions drift' problem.
Mike: love it. can you paste the template here?
Ana: sure, pulled it from the meeting notes. it's intentionally short so engineers actually fill it out.
Ana: ```
T+0  (Incident): declare, add short summary + impact metrics, IC assigned
T+1  (24h)   : initial RCA draft + raw logs linked
T+3  (72h)   : action items assigned with owners + due dates (sprint ticket + label:pmr-action)
T+7         : owner status update in thread (what's blocked / ETA)
T+14        : follow-up sync (15m) — IC + owners + eng lead, confirm mitigations
T+30        : recurrence check + close or re-escalate
```
Li: short and actionable — nice. propose adding an explicit 'risk of recurrence' score at T+3 so we prioritise fixes.
Samir: +1 for risk scoring. also, can we add a simple comms cadence: who posts the T+7 update and where? some orgs miss it.
Ana: good call. my suggestion: owners post T+7 in the same slack thread and update the PMR doc header; if owner is unavailable, the IC or oncall backup posts.
Mike: for rotation, can we formalize IC backup? i.e., define a two-week IC rotation and a named backup so follow-ups don't stall.
Samir: yes — propose 2-week IC rotations, backup assigned, and a recurring calendar event that auto-adds owners for T+14 review.
Li: small nit: add a single field in the PMR for 'blocked_by' and links to blockers (PRs, infra tickets). makes T+7 terse.
Ana: agreed. also adding a short template for ownership that can be pasted into the postmortem:
Ana: ```
Action: enable-prefix-cache for inference cache
Owner: @Samir
Due: 2026-04-07
Blocked_by: infra/PR-432
Risk: high
Status: in-progress
```
Samir: I can pilot this on the last incident. will create sprint tickets for my actions and post updates here every T+7.
incident-bot: reminder set — T+7 follow-up ping will be posted 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC for thread 2166543210
Mike: one process ask — can we add a small metric column to the PMR header (p50 tail, error-rate delta) so follow-ups can validate improvements?
Ana: done. I'll update the org PMR template and drop a one-pager in docs with the timeline + comms cadence.
Li: can you also add a short checklist for when to escalate to 'repeat incident review' (>=2 similar incidents in 30d)?
Ana: yup — my rule: if we see recurrence pattern twice in 30d or once with large customer impact, schedule a deep review and exec summary.
Samir: ok i'm on owner duties. will post first T+7 update here.
Mike: thanks — let's try this flow on the next PMR. small, measurable changes. :thumbsup:
